newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian mobile phone deal overpriced-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Austrian mobile phone deal overpriced-analysts.

text.p: Austria's postal and telecoms monopoly PTA on Wednesday sold a 25 percent stake in its mobile phone unit to Italy's Stet for 8.4 billion schillings ($700 million) in a deal some analysts said was overpriced.
"It's definitely a good move for Stet which needs foreign exposure. My only reservation is that the price paid seems high," said William Laurent, a telecoms analyst at brokerage Robert Fleming.
He said he would put the total value of Mobilkom at about two billion dollars, given its current client base of 400,000 subscribers in Austria's population of eight million.
PTA finance chief Johannes Ditz admitted earlier that the size of the offer had come as a surprise to the company.
"The price reflects the market possibilities Stet sees in Austria and the potential for synergies," he said. "It also reflects the dominant position of Mobilkom Austria in the Austrian market."
Ditz said Mobilkom had put in a strong performance since the unit was set up in 1996, despite the presence of a competitor in the market.
He predicted the unit would post a pre-tax profit of up to one billion schillings in 1996 and a net profit of 500 million.

Evan Miller, an analyst at CSFB, said the deal was beneficial to both parties. "It gives Stet access to a very well-developed and successful wireless network and PTA is undoubtedly happy with the bid they received," he said.

Stet had been competing against rival offers from Tele Danmark, the Unicom unit of the international Unisource alliance, and South Western Bell of the U.S, whose offers were reported to have been substantially below Stet's.
Mobilkom operates Austria's biggest global system for mobile communications (GSM) network. Its chief rival is max.mobil, which is owned by a private consortium.

Stet managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said in a statement released in Rome the company expected mobile phones to account for one quarter of the Austrian telephone market by the year 2000, from 8.75 percent currently.

"Stet has ambitious targets but I think the market will grow pretty rapidly," analyst Jim Ross at ABN Amro Hoare Govett said. He estimated that within 15 to 20 years mobile phones would constitute 50 percent of the telecoms market in Europe.
But Fleming's Laurent deemed Stet's forecast unrealistic.

"The figure of 25 percent seems to me to be very optimistic indeed," he said. "Mobile tariffs are very high in Austria and with competition from abroad I believe prices will have to come down," he said.

The Austrian government plans to award a third mobile phone licence this summer to boost competition ahead of the planned liberalisation of the Austrian telecommunications sector in 1998, one year before PTA's scheduled privatisation.
